metadata.name: Kantian Republicanism
metadata.description: A juridical republican tradition grounding civil freedom in public law, representative government and a voluntary federation directed toward lasting peace.
metadata.scope: Kant’s original juridical republicanism and federation for peace, retaining its historical restrictive active-citizenship rule and rejection of revolution; modern equal suffrage is not silently substituted. This is a provisional, scoped interpretation, not a survey of adherents. Modern applications and five-point intensities are inferred. The cited sources establish context; they do not document answers to every quiz statement.
metadata.phrase: Society should protect equal civil freedom through representative public law and cooperate in a voluntary federation that restrains war while preserving states’ legal independence.
